title: Prime Minister holds official talks on his State Visit to Uzbekistan
body_text:
As part of his State Visit to Uzbekistan, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today held official talks with the President of Uzbekistan, H.E. Mr. Shavkat Mirziyoyev. On arrival at the Kuksaroy Presidential Palace, Prime Minister was warmly received by President Mirziyoyev and accorded a ceremonial welcome. He conveyed his warmest wishes to Uzbekistan on the occasion of their 35th anniversary of Independence.
The two leaders held wide-ranging and substantive discussions in delegation level format on the entire gamut of the bilateral strategic partnership, including trade and investment, innovation and start-up, digital public infrastructure and UPI, defence and security, healthcare and pharmaceuticals, critical minerals, agriculture, education, tourism, agriculture, space and people-to-people exchanges. Prime Minister appreciated the progress made in the long-term arrangement for supply of Uranium from Uzbekistan to India and reaffirmed the importance of strengthening cooperation in critical minerals. Reflecting the depth and salience of the relationship, they decided to elevate the bilateral Strategic Partnership to the level of Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. They also agreed to set a bilateral trade target of USD 5 billion by 2030 and in this regard called for hosting a Business Summit to deepen economic and investment ties. To take forward the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in a meaningful manner, the two leaders agreed to set up a Foreign Ministers led mechanism and raise the Inter-Governmental Commission to the ministerial level.
The leaders noted that ancient civilizational linkages and contemporary people-to-people ties continue to add vitality to the partnership. In this regard, Prime Minister appreciated the popularity of Yoga in Uzbekistan. Earlier in the day, he viewed a Yoga Session organised by the Yoga Federation of Uzbekistan. To commemorate the 60th anniversary of the passing of former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri, Prime Minister Modi announced the Lal Bahadur Shastri Scholarship for Hindi language for Uzbek students . Recognising the convergence between Uzbekistan’s “Yashil Makon” green initiative and India’s “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative, Prime Minister Modi announced India’s partnership with Uzbekistan in the ongoing environmental rehabilitation efforts in the Aral Sea region with a grant of USD 1 million for the project. The two leaders also jointly planted a tree in the Palace garden.
Following the talks, the two sides witnessed the exchange of MoUs and agreements covering a wide range of areas, including culture, higher education and research, capacity building, archives, economic collaboration, environment, tourism, mining, ayurveda and sister-state relations. A Letter of Intent for the restoration of the Buddhist sites of Fayaz Tepa and Kara Tepa in Uzbekistan was concluded. An MoU for the establishment of an ICCR Sanskrit Chair at the Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies was also finalised. The full list of MoUs and agreements can be accessed here .
President Mirziyoyev hosted a banquet lunch in honour of Prime Minister. Prime Minister thanked President Mirziyoyev for his gracious hospitality and invited him to visit India.

enrichment.summary: During PM Modi's State Visit to Uzbekistan, he and President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held bilateral talks and decided to elevate their Strategic Partnership to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. They set a bilateral trade target of USD 5 billion by 2030, agreed to establish a Foreign Ministers-led mechanism and raise the Inter-Governmental Commission to ministerial level, and signed multiple MoUs covering culture, education, mining, environment and tourism. India also announced a USD 1 million grant for Aral Sea rehabilitation and a Lal Bahadur Shastri Scholarship for Hindi language studies in Uzbekistan.
enrichment.context:
India-Uzbekistan relations have grown steadily since the 1990s, with cooperation expanding into strategic areas including uranium supply for India's nuclear program, defence, and connectivity via the International North-South Transport Corridor. Uzbekistan is a key Central Asian partner for India under its 'Connect Central Asia' policy, and this visit reflects India's push to deepen ties in a region where China and Russia have traditionally had greater influence. The elevation to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership signals an upgrade in institutional mechanisms for engagement, similar to upgrades India has made with other strategic partners.

The visit also carries civilizational and cultural dimensions, referencing shared Buddhist heritage (restoration of Fayaz Tepa and Kara Tepa sites) and India's soft power initiatives like ICCR Sanskrit Chairs and Yoga diplomacy. The critical minerals and uranium cooperation is significant given India's efforts to diversify supply chains for nuclear fuel and strategic minerals amid global geopolitical uncertainties. However, this release is primarily a descriptive account of a diplomatic visit with announcements of intent (trade targets, MoUs) rather than a landmark policy shift, though the partnership upgrade itself has some substantive value for foreign relations tracking.

prelims_questions.question: During PM Modi's 2026 State Visit to Uzbekistan, the bilateral Strategic Partnership between India and Uzbekistan was elevated to which level?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that the two leaders decided to elevate the bilateral Strategic Partnership to the level of Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following was announced by India during PM Modi's visit to Uzbekistan?
options: USD 1 million grant for Aral Sea rehabilitation
USD 10 million grant for uranium mining
Establishment of an IIT campus in Tashkent
A free trade agreement between India and Uzbekistan
prelims_questions.explanation: PM Modi announced a USD 1 million grant for environmental rehabilitation efforts in the Aral Sea region, linking Uzbekistan's 'Yashil Makon' initiative with India's 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' initiative.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the strategic significance of India's growing partnership with Uzbekistan and Central Asian nations in the context of energy security and critical mineral supply chains.
Examine the role of cultural and civilizational linkages in strengthening India's bilateral relations with Central Asian countries, citing recent examples.

study_notes.reason: The release's chief value is the diplomatic significance of elevating India-Uzbekistan ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and the strategic rationale (critical minerals, uranium, Central Asia outreach) rather than any dense factual core worth memorising.

prelims.point: India-Uzbekistan Strategic Partnership was elevated to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership during PM Modi's 2024 State Visit
prelims.why_important: Naming and dating bilateral partnership upgrades is a classic prelims fact-matching item (Strategic vs Comprehensive Strategic Partnership terminology).

prelims.point: Bilateral trade target of USD 5 billion set between India and Uzbekistan for 2030
prelims.why_important: Specific numeric targets in bilateral agreements are sometimes tested as factual recall.

prelims.point: Lal Bahadur Shastri Scholarship for Hindi language announced for Uzbek students, marking 60th anniversary of Shastri's death
prelims.why_important: Links a soft-power initiative to a historical commemoration, a pattern UPSC uses to test static-current linkages.

prelims.point: India announced USD 1 million grant for Aral Sea rehabilitation, linked to convergence of Uzbekistan's 'Yashil Makon' and India's 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' initiatives
prelims.why_important: Tests awareness of India's environmental diplomacy and specific named schemes used in bilateral cooperation.

prelims.point: ICCR Sanskrit Chair established at Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies; restoration MoU for Buddhist sites Fayaz Tepa and Kara Tepa
prelims.why_important: Cultural diplomacy specifics (named institutions/sites) are the kind of detail UPSC uses in match-the-following prelims questions.

mains.point: Uranium supply arrangement from Uzbekistan and enhanced critical minerals cooperation reflect India's strategy to diversify nuclear fuel and strategic mineral supply chains
mains.analytical_use: Useful for questions on India's energy security strategy or diversification of critical mineral/nuclear fuel imports amid geopolitical uncertainty.

mains.point: Elevation to Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and new ministerial-level mechanisms (Foreign Ministers-led body, upgraded Inter-Governmental Commission) signal deeper institutionalisation of India-Central Asia engagement
mains.analytical_use: Deployable in 'Discuss/Analyse India's Connect Central Asia policy and its strategic significance' type questions, citing institutional upgrades as evidence of deepening ties.

mains.point: Visit reflects India's competitive positioning vis-à-vis China and Russia's traditional influence in Central Asia
mains.analytical_use: Supports answers on great-power competition in Central Asia and India's balancing strategy.

mains.point: Use of cultural and civilizational diplomacy (Buddhist heritage restoration, Sanskrit Chair, Yoga diplomacy) as soft-power tools to consolidate strategic partnerships
mains.analytical_use: Useful for 'Role of cultural diplomacy in strengthening India's bilateral relations' type analytical questions.

low_priority.reason: Symbolic gesture without substantive policy content.
